_comment: Week-one water gate thresholds. Changing a number here is a reviewable diff; changing it in code is not. The checker reads this file and nothing else.
_verified: Unity 6.3 LTS = 6000.3 (released 2025-12-04, supported through 2027-12). com.unity.test-framework.performance 3.6.0 is the version released for the 6000.0 stream; take what Package Manager tags Recommended for your editor build.
_units: All timings are MILLISECONDS PER SOLVER STEP, not per frame. Scenario C takes 3600 steps per sample and the harness divides by 3600, so C is directly comparable with A and B. The frame-level question is answered by multiplying: at 30 Hz a frame is 33.33 ms, and the solver's share of it is the per-step figure times the number of steps that frame takes.

hard_fail._comment: These are NOT budget failures. The ladder buys performance and cannot buy correctness. Halving the resolution of a broken solver produces a broken solver that is twice as fast.
hard_fail._mass_note: The mass check is a BALANCE, not a constancy check: the checker compares mass_after against mass_before + mass_inflow. A field with an open source is supposed to gain water, so asserting constant mass would fail a correct solver and pass a dry one.
hard_fail._determinism_note: Scenario D_Determinism is asserted in NUnit, not here. A red test case in the results XML is treated as a hard fail by the checker, which is how a determinism break reaches the verdict.

ladder.action: Halve the simulation resolution to 129. No visible loss - the render grid is unchanged.
Shrink the active water window to the tiles within 1 of the camera.
Channel graph on Android only. A real gameplay difference.
ladder.cost: Android water is not freely redirectable

ladder.action: Delay the Android tier. NOT the design.
Water stops being redirectable. Revisit Deliverable 1.
